summary: Remap a cylindrical velocity distribution between two phase-space meshes. The default branch preserves nonnegativity and spatially interpolated discrete density, axial momentum density and squared-speed energy density through a constrained relative-entropy projection; unrealizable destination moments fail explicitly.

identity.relation: nonnegative finite-grid remap with three extensive-moment constraints
identity.direction: nonnegative distribution and two normalized cylindrical phase-space meshes -> conservative destination distribution, or a typed infeasibility/convergence failure
identity.definition: Let w_ij = pi*(r_right^2-r_left^2)*dvx and fV = sqrt(Tnorm_b/Tnorm_a). On source nodes form M_a = sum w_a*fa*(1, vx_a/fV, (vr_a/fV)^2+(vx_a/fV)^2). At each destination x, linearly interpolate these three extensive moments first. For n=M_0>0, find cell probabilities p>=0, sum p=1, E_p[vx_b]=M_1/n and E_p[vr_b^2+vx_b^2]=M_2/n, minimizing sum p*log(p/q). q mixes 1e-12 normalized cell-volume probability with normalized overlap masses on the feasible face. Return fb=n*p/w_b. Zero density gives zero; identical velocity grids and normalization use convex spatial interpolation directly.
identity.model: stateless two-velocity/one-spatial-axis cell-overlap remap followed by a nonnegative relative-entropy projection; scientific correction of the saved AN/BN algorithm, not corrected-branch source parity
identity.geometry: two velocity dimensions over one spatial axis, per phase-space mesh
identity.coordinates: velocity nodes and distributions in the source normalized units, spatial nodes in m; Tnorm in eV
identity.boundary: finite real strictly increasing axes with at least two nodes; nonnegative radial axes and two-sided axial axes; retained velocity-node and spatial overlap checks; finite positive Tnorm and representable scale ratio; aligned finite fa, nonnegative for correct=1; target mean velocity/energy must lie in the destination-node convex hull and the binary64 calculation must meet its return postcondition
assumptions: The operator is stateless and recomputes cell-overlap weights per call; source cache lifecycle and whole KN1D state are outside the contract.

Cylindrical cell volumes are pi*(r_right^2-r_left^2)*dvx, using the shared SciRel quadrature. Conserved momentum and energy are discrete node moments, not analytic integrals over a continuous reconstructed distribution.

Source normalization is converted with fV=sqrt(Tnorm_b/Tnorm_a). Density, axial momentum density and squared-speed energy density are spatially interpolated before division by density; interpolating mean velocity or mean energy would be wrong when density varies.

For correct=1, finite nonnegative input is required. Positive reference probability (1e-12 cell-volume mixture) can put mass in previously zero-overlap cells; it selects a realizable entropy projection without relaxing moments, clipping negative output or preserving all higher moments.

Realizable normalized targets lie in conv{(vx_j, vr_i^2+vx_j^2)}. Targets on a face use only that face. Scaled geometric classification uses 64 binary64 eps; the final distribution must satisfy all three scaled moment residuals within 128 eps.

Damped Newton solves the entropy dual, with covariance Hessian and stable log-sum-exp. max_correction_iterations caps updates per spatial slice (default 1000); infeasibility and numerical nonconvergence are distinct failures, neither returns a partial distribution.
Zero-density slices are zero. Equal velocity grids and equal Tnorm use convex spatial interpolation and preserve identity at common spatial nodes; out-of-domain spatial nodes are zero-filled.

correct=0 retains the historical algebraic interpolation and conditional density rescale, including signed inputs. It does not provide the default branch's positivity or three-moment physical guarantee.

The corrected mathematical remap intentionally changes the defective source correction. Historical source comparison, withdrawn strict KN1DPy D1 status, external atomic-physics oracle gaps and pending public licensing are not erased by this repair.

inputs.name: fa
inputs.constraints: Finite real aligned three-dimensional array; nonnegative for correct=1. Signed finite inputs remain accepted only by the algebraic correct=0 branch. Boolean, string and complex coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: vr_a
inputs.constraints: Finite real, nonnegative, strictly increasing, at least two nodes.

inputs.name: vx_a
inputs.constraints: Finite real, strictly increasing, at least two nodes, covering negative and positive axial velocities.

inputs.name: x_a
inputs.constraints: Finite real, strictly increasing, at least two nodes.

inputs.name: Tnorm_a
inputs.constraints: Finite real and strictly positive; the ratio to Tnorm_b must yield a finite positive velocity scale.

inputs.name: vr_b
inputs.constraints: Finite real, nonnegative, strictly increasing, at least two nodes.

inputs.name: vx_b
inputs.constraints: Finite real, strictly increasing, at least two nodes, covering negative and positive axial velocities.

inputs.name: x_b
inputs.constraints: Finite real, strictly increasing, at least two nodes.

inputs.name: Tnorm_b
inputs.constraints: Finite real and strictly positive; the ratio to Tnorm_a must yield a finite positive velocity scale.

inputs.name: correct
inputs.constraints: Integer 1 applies nonnegative conservative entropy projection; integer 0 retains the algebraic interpolation plus historical conditional density rescale without the physical moment guarantee. Boolean and coercible selectors are rejected.

inputs.name: do_warn
inputs.constraints: None (default) skips warnings; an integer applies the saved do_warn * max(fb) threshold without changing output. Other selector types are rejected.

inputs.name: max_correction_iterations
inputs.description: Maximum damped-Newton updates per target spatial node.
inputs.constraints: Positive integer; numerical exhaustion raises MomentCorrectionConvergenceError (a ValueError subclass) with no partial result. An unrealizable target instead raises InfeasibleMomentsError independently of this budget.

outputs.name: fb
outputs.constraints: For correct=1: finite nonnegative distribution with discrete density, axial momentum density and squared-speed energy density matching the spatially interpolated source targets to scaled roundoff; zero outside the source x interval. correct=0 is a finite algebraic result without that physical guarantee.

preconditions: Both meshes satisfy the declared axes, shape, overlap and representability contracts.
For correct=1, fa is nonnegative and each nonzero-density target moment lies inside the convex hull of destination velocity/energy nodes.
supported: Nonuniform cylindrical velocity meshes, nonzero axial drift, unequal normalization temperatures and spatially varying density.
Simultaneous discrete density, axial momentum density and squared-speed energy-density conservation with nonnegative output in the default branch.
Zero density, equal-grid identity, convex spatial interpolation, exact hull edges/vertices and explicit infeasibility diagnostics.
Retained stateless correct=0 compatibility and unchanged boundary-warning selector.
excluded: Remapping a physically unrealizable moment target on a finite destination grid; no clipping, target relaxation or silent enlargement is performed.
Missing retained velocity-node/spatial overlap, two-dimensional spatial grids or three velocity dimensions.
Guaranteed preservation of higher moments, detailed distribution shape or entropy; the entropy objective chooses among feasible three-moment distributions.
Atomic-physics validation, complete KN1D capability and source cache-state equivalence.
A physical conservation or positivity claim for the signed algebraic correct=0 branch.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for invalid axis/shape/real-type/temperature/selector/overlap contracts or negative fa in correct=1. InfeasibleMomentsError, a ValueError subclass, reports an unrealizable destination moment with x_b index, requested normalized means, maximum node energy and a separating-inequality residual.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError for nonrepresentable quadrature, overlap, source moments or final values. MomentCorrectionConvergenceError, a ValueError subclass, reports an unresolved hull face, singular covariance, missing descent/line-search step or failed finite nonnegative three-moment return postcondition.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: The state is the entropy-dual parameter on the feasible hull face. Each bounded update computes moment residual and covariance Hessian, then takes a damped Newton step (at most 64 line-search trials). Stop when the scaled moment residual is at most 32 binary64 eps; return also requires the actual output three-moment postcondition within 128 eps. Exceeding max_correction_iterations updates per spatial slice raises MomentCorrectionConvergenceError with its index; infeasible targets use a separate error.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; any rejected spatial slice aborts the call without a partial distribution or input mutation.

python.signature: interp_distribution_across_mesh(fa, vr_a, vx_a, x_a, Tnorm_a, vr_b, vx_b, x_b, Tnorm_b, correct=1, do_warn=None, max_correction_iterations=1000)

example.description: Transfer a drifting distribution with spatially varying density; check nonnegativity and all three independently assembled discrete moments.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import interp_distribution_across_mesh

def moments(f, r, v, T):
    re = np.r_[0.0, (r[:-1] + r[1:]) / 2, r[-1] + (r[-1] - r[-2]) / 2]
    ve = np.r_[v[0] - (v[1] - v[0]) / 2, (v[:-1] + v[1:]) / 2, v[-1] + (v[-1] - v[-2]) / 2]
    mass = f * (np.pi * np.diff(re**2)[:, None] * np.diff(ve)[None, :])[:, :, None]
    return np.array([mass.sum(axis=(0, 1)),
                     (mass * (np.sqrt(T) * v)[None, :, None]).sum(axis=(0, 1)),
                     (mass * (T * (r[:, None]**2 + v[None, :]**2))[:, :, None]).sum(axis=(0, 1))])

ra, va, xa = np.linspace(0.5, 2.0, 4), np.linspace(-1.5, 1.5, 6), np.linspace(0, 1, 5)
rb, vb, xb = np.linspace(0.1, 2.8, 8), np.linspace(-2.7, 2.7, 11), np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, 4)
fa = np.exp(-ra[:, None, None]**2 - (va[None, :, None] - 0.3)**2) * (1 + 2 * xa)[None, None, :]
fb = interp_distribution_across_mesh(fa, ra, va, xa, 2.0, rb, vb, xb, 1.5)
source = moments(fa, ra, va, 2.0)
expected = np.array([np.interp(xb, xa, row) for row in source])
actual = moments(fb, rb, vb, 1.5)
assert fb.shape == (8, 11, 4) and np.isfinite(fb).all() and np.all(fb >= 0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(actual, expected, rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-13)
print(actual)
example.expected: A finite nonnegative array of shape (8,11,4). Independently assembled density, axial momentum density and squared-speed energy density match the spatially interpolated source profiles at rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-13. This is a discrete remap example, not an atomic-physics validation.

scope: Original positive-input negative-output failure is retained as RED evidence; a convex-hull energy bound proves the first two original-grid targets impossible, and the corrected API explicitly rejects them.
The same random positive input on a wider feasible grid and the original feasible two-slice tail return nonnegative distributions with all three independently integrated moments.
Independent scalar cylindrical quadrature checks nonuniform grids, nonzero drift, unequal temperatures and interpolation of extensive moments when spatial density varies.
Exact zero-density and equal-grid identity/convex spatial interpolation are checked, including outside-source spatial zero fill.
Lower/upper convex-hull edges, a vertex and a near-face interior target are checked without clipping or relaxing targets.
Input rejection, distinct infeasibility versus bounded numerical exhaustion, input immutability, deterministic repetition and retained correct=0/warning behavior are checked.

The retained numerical assertions and new scientific regressions run with the quadrature dependencies; selected-wheel runtime is independently checked without source, pytest, reference answers or network.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Author candidate evidence establishes a finite-grid nonnegative three-moment remap and explicit unrealizability/iteration failures in the tested domain, including a source-free selected-wheel runtime. Independent root acceptance, human scientific endorsement and release licensing remain separate. It does not rehabilitate withdrawn KN1DPy D1 provenance, reproduce corrected source arrays, establish all continuous-distribution moments, or validate atomic physics.
known_limitations: The historical KN1DPy strict D1 qualification remains withdrawn; this mathematical successor is not full source-project replacement.
Finite destination nodes can make requested moments unrealizable; the caller must provide a feasible grid or handle InfeasibleMomentsError.
The entropy prior includes a 1e-12 cell-volume mixture and may populate zero-overlap cells. Higher moments and fine distribution shape are not conserved by the three-moment constraints.
Binary64 conditioning, very near hull faces and unrepresentable intermediates can cause explicit numerical failure; the iteration budget is not a universal convergence guarantee.
correct=0 is retained algebraic compatibility only and does not carry the default branch physical guarantees.
Public distribution licensing and human scientific endorsement remain pending.
